messages:
Dylan Brooks: Heads up: early dogfood feedback on the route-level A/B testing Console flow is pretty rough. Folks are confused about Start vs Stop vs Rollback, and the copy doesn’t make it obvious what traffic is doing.

Chloe Martin: +1. I tried it in staging and I had to click around to figure out if it was actually sending 10% to B. The status pill says “Active” but then there’s a “Stop experiment” button and a separate “Rollback” in the overflow menu. I wasn’t sure what each does.

Kenji Nakamura: Yeah, in the prototype we had “Pause” not “Stop” and we lost that nuance when we went to implementation. Current labels imply “Stop = revert to control”, but it’s actually “Stop = freeze assignment + route goes back to baseline policy”, right?

Jordan Lee: Implementation-wise today:
- Start: enables the routing policy + assignment
- Stop: disables the experiment policy (route goes back to non-experiment routing)
- Rollback: sets allocation to 100/0 and marks B disabled, but leaves experiment record “running” (so exposures keep logging for control)

Jordan Lee: Which… is very unintuitive. :grimacing:

Tessa Morgan: That’s exactly the mismatch in mental model. People read “Rollback” as “undo everything / restore previous config”.

Marissa Cole: We need to pick semantics + make them explicit in UI.
I’d prefer:
- Draft (not serving)
- Running (serving split)
- Paused (not serving split, config preserved)
- Stopped (ended, can’t restart?)
And “Rollback” should be “Set traffic to control (100%)” with guardrails.

Chloe Martin: Also, validation step is unclear. It says “Config valid” but doesn’t show *what* it validated. Dogfooders asked: “Did it check model availability in region? did it check I’m not overlapping with a canary?”

Leila Farouk: From QA side: we’ve had 3 separate questions from internal dogfood:
1) “Start” confirmation should show exact split + hash key + which route it applies to.
2) “Stop” should warn that results will have a discontinuity (no more exposures).
3) If you edit allocation while running, should show that it takes effect immediately and may impact metrics comparisons.

Dylan Brooks: Yep. One quote from Solutions: “I’m scared to click anything because I can’t tell if it’s going to send 50% of prod traffic to a new model.”

Allison Grant: For ops, we need clear warnings when guardrails are not configured / not active. Like a banner: “No automatic rollback configured” or “Guardrail evaluator running every 60s; rollback triggers at +15% p95 latency or +0.5% error rate”.

Kenji Nakamura: Copy suggestion:
- Primary CTA: “Start experiment” (only in Draft)
- While Running: show “Traffic split live: A 90% / B 10%” above the fold
- Replace “Stop experiment” with “Pause experiment” (keeps config, stops splitting traffic)
- “End experiment” behind overflow w/ stronger confirmation
- Replace “Rollback” with “Route all traffic to A (control)” (and keep experiment running for measurement)

Marissa Cole: + add an “Explain” tooltip: “Pausing stops assigning variants; requests will follow baseline routing. Experiment results will exclude paused window.”

Chloe Martin: Another confusion point: variant naming. Right now it’s “Variant A / Variant B” everywhere. People asked for “Control / Treatment” labels (at least as an option) and a place to add a description.

Dylan Brooks: We also need better “what’s happening” on the Results tab. Right now it’s empty until aggregation job catches up, so people think it’s broken.

Leila Farouk: Could we add a skeleton state: “Processing results (up to ~5 min)” + last refresh timestamp.

Allison Grant: And a link to the dashboard / “View in Grafana” once enabled. Dogfooders want to sanity check.

Connor O'Brien: Release note: if we change semantics (Stop vs Pause), we need to coordinate with enablement + docs. But better to fix now before beta partners see it.

Tessa Morgan: I can take a pass on revised microcopy + confirmation modals today. Need input from Eng on the exact behavior we can commit to for v1.

Jordan Lee: I’ll write up the current semantics + recommended changes and post in the design issue. I’d strongly vote we align behavior with labels (Pause should not mutate allocation; Rollback should be explicit 100% to control).

Marissa Cole: Action items:
- Kenji/Tessa: propose updated button labels + warning copy (esp Start/Pause/End/Route-to-control)
- Chloe/Jordan: confirm backend can support “Pause” state vs “Stop” as distinct
- Allison: list the minimum guardrail warnings we must surface in Console
Let’s aim to land copy changes + confirmation modal in the next dogfood build.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: I’ll collect the dogfood notes and paste them into the Linear ticket + link this thread.
